ordered_diagnoses: Drug-induced liver injury with associated skin manifestations

candidates.name: Drug-induced liver injury with associated skin manifestations
support_spans: 7 days of yellow scleral discoloration
Two days after starting ciprofloxacin, he developed generalized pruritus that progressed to fluid-filled rashes
AST 283 U/L, ALT 246 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 1390 U/L
Total bilirubin 14 mg/dL (conjugated 13.7 mg/dL)
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of jaundice, elevated liver enzymes, and skin lesions following the use of ciprofloxacin suggest a diagnosis of drug-induced liver injury with associated skin manifestations.

candidates.name: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
support_spans: generalized painful fluid‐filled skin lesions

candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of widespread skin lesions and recent medication use are consistent with acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis.

candidates.name: Drug-induced liver injury
support_spans: he developed a surgical-site infection and persistent fever; he initially took paracetamol without relief, then obtained ciprofloxacin over the counter. Two days after starting ciprofloxacin, he developed generalized pruritus that progressed to fluid-filled rashes.
AST 283 U/L, ALT 246 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 1390 U/L
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results are consistent with liver injury, which could be caused by the use of ciprofloxacin.

candidates.name: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
support_spans: he developed generalized pruritus that progressed to fluid-filled rashes.
Dermatologic examination showed multiple generalized vesicles and bullae with non-hemorrhagic crusts over the trunk and extremities (palms and soles spared).
candidates.why: The patient's skin lesions and mucosal findings are consistent with Stevens-Johnson syndrome, a severe skin and mucous membrane disorder.

candidates.name: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
support_spans: he developed generalized pruritus that progressed to fluid-filled rashes.
Leukocyte count 18,520/mm3 (neutrophils 64%, lymphocytes 22%, eosinophils 12%)
candidates.why: The patient's skin lesions and elevated eosinophil count are consistent with acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, a skin condition characterized by a sudden onset of pustules.

selector.runner_up: Drug-induced liver injury with associated skin manifestations
selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of generalized painful fluid-filled skin lesions and the temporal relationship with ciprofloxacin use are most consistent with acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, which is supported by the presence of eosinophilia and the lack of systemic symptoms such as fever at the time of examination.

rejected.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has mucosal involvement and skin lesions, the lack of systemic symptoms such as fever at the time of examination and the presence of eosinophilia make Stevens-Johnson syndrome less likely.
